LESSON: READING POSTURE

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 3.6: Reading Posture

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Reading Posture
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: What is appropriate Posture learner should be able to: correct reading posture after observing a reading posture?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. Demonstrate appropriate demonstration on sitting properly when picture 2.
2. Identify correct reading poems and rhymes related to appropriate reading postures in pictures or in class. posture
3. Identify incorrect reading • Learners could be exposed to models of correct postures in pictures or in class. reading posture

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Reading Posture

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Reading Posture

Teach
• Focus skill: Demonstrate appropriate demonstration on sitting properly when picture 2..
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Reading Posture.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Reading Posture
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is appropriate Posture learner should be able to: correct reading posture after observing a reading posture?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
